prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): it calls `json.loads` on any string-valued argument whose annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts string parameters typed as a union (e.g. `str | None`) when the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON object/array passed as a literal string). Both PRs change the same condition in `pre_parse_json` to skip pre-parsing for such union annotations, adding a new helper function to decide when parsing is safe. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): it calls `json.loads` on any string-valued argument whose annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts string parameters typed as a union (e.g. `str | None`) when the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON object/array passed as a literal string). Both PRs change the same condition in `pre_parse_json` to skip pre-parsing for such union annotations, adding a new helper function to decide when parsing is safe. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` tests union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str, int, float, bool, NoneType) without unwrapping `Annotated`. This means the very common idiom `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` still fails the 'simple types' check (an `Annotated[...]` object doesn't match any entry in `_SIMPLE_TYPES`), so pre-parsing still runs and the original corruption bug persists for Field-annotated optional string parameters. PR #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and applies it before checking union members in `_is_optional_str`, so it correctly detects and fixes the bug for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, in addition to plain `str | None`. #2032's broader 'any simple-type union' heuristic (also covering `str | int`, `str | bool`, etc.) could be folded into #3056's narrower, annotation-aware helper if that broader coverage is still wanted.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` tests union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str, int, float, bool, NoneType) without unwrapping `Annotated`. This means the very common idiom `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` still fails the 'simple types' check (an `Annotated[...]` object doesn't match any entry in `_SIMPLE_TYPES`), so pre-parsing still runs and the original corruption bug persists for Field-annotated optional string parameters. PR #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and applies it before checking union members in `_is_optional_str`, so it correctly detects and fixes the bug for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, in addition to plain `str | None`. #2032's broader 'any simple-type union' heuristic (also covering `str | int`, `str | bool`, etc.) could be folded into #3056's narrower, annotation-aware helper if that broader coverage is still wanted.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: Both fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): it calls `json.loads` on any string-valued argument whose annotation is not exactly `str`, which corrupts string parameters typed as a union (e.g. `str | None`) when the string happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON object/array passed as a literal string). clusters.pick_reason: #2654 is a minimal, targeted fix (buffer size 0->1 plus a comment) against the current codebase using create_context_streams, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the actual handler-blocks-during-progress-notification scenario. #2215 is based on an older version of the file (still calls anyio.create_memory_object_stream directly rather than the create_context_streams helper used in #2552/#2654), so it no longer applies cleanly and would need a rebase/merge-conflict resolution. #2215 also only adds configurable buffer-size parameters defaulting to 0, so it does not change default behavior and would not fix the blocking bug unless every caller opts in by passing write_stream_buffer_size=1 — #2654 fixes it out of the box for all callers with a smaller diff.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the exhaustion branch directly in _handle_reconnection: it detects the specific in-flight JSONRPCRequest via ctx.session_message.message and sends a scoped JSONRPCError(INTERNAL_ERROR) through ctx.read_stream_writer, unblocking only that pending call while leaving the rest of the session/task group intact. #3098 instead adds a generic _unwrap_exception helper that walks an exception's `.exceptions` tree to find a StreamableHTTPError and re-raise it, which implies the failure propagates as a raised exception out of the task group — a broader blast radius that tears down the whole client context rather than resolving just the affected request, and it does not special-case JSONRPCRequest vs. other message types the way #2395 does. #3098's diff also carries an unrelated revert of `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to a plain import, unrelated to the reconnection fix itself.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` tests union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str, int, float, bool, NoneType) without unwrapping `Annotated`. This means the very common idiom `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` still fails the 'simple types' check (an `Annotated[...]` object doesn't match any entry in `_SIMPLE_TYPES`), so pre-parsing still runs and the original corruption bug persists for Field-annotated optional string parameters. PR #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` and applies it before checking union members in `_is_optional_str`, so it correctly detects and fixes the bug for `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`, in addition to plain `str | None`. #2032's broader 'any simple-type union' heuristic (also covering `str | int`, `str | bool`, etc.) could be folded into #3056's narrower, annotation-aware helper if that broader coverage is still wanted.

clusters.pick_reason: #2654 is a minimal, targeted fix (buffer size 0->1 plus a comment) against the current codebase using create_context_streams, and ships a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the actual handler-blocks-during-progress-notification scenario. #2215 is based on an older version of the file (still calls anyio.create_memory_object_stream directly rather than the create_context_streams helper used in #2552/#2654), so it no longer applies cleanly and would need a rebase/merge-conflict resolution. #2215 also only adds configurable buffer-size parameters defaulting to 0, so it does not change default behavior and would not fix the blocking bug unless every caller opts in by passing write_stream_buffer_size=1 — #2654 fixes it out of the box for all callers with a smaller diff.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the exhaustion branch directly in _handle_reconnection: it detects the specific in-flight JSONRPCRequest via ctx.session_message.message and sends a scoped JSONRPCError(INTERNAL_ERROR) through ctx.read_stream_writer, unblocking only that pending call while leaving the rest of the session/task group intact. #3098 instead adds a generic _unwrap_exception helper that walks an exception's `.exceptions` tree to find a StreamableHTTPError and re-raise it, which implies the failure propagates as a raised exception out of the task group — a broader blast radius that tears down the whole client context rather than resolving just the affected request, and it does not special-case JSONRPCRequest vs. other message types the way #2395 does. #3098's diff also carries an unrelated revert of `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` back to a plain import, unrelated to the reconnection fix itself.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add functionally equivalent quote/escape-aware comma splitters (_iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041), but #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which isolates the Bearer scheme's own auth-params before matching. This also handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=...'), where #3012's approach tokenizes the whole header as one flat param list without scheme disambiguation and would still be susceptible to picking up a same-named parameter from a different scheme's challenge.
